quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #22
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right where you see this sign.

questions.question: What do some highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows mark the lanes for specific uses, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System loses traction on a slippery road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press down hard on the brake pedal and keep holding it. The ABS system will pump the brakes for you faster than you could manually. Do not pump the brakes yourself or release the pedal, as this will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine by moving the ignition switch just enough to stop it. Be careful not to move it too far, as this will lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System, what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Firmly pump your brakes.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly pump your brakes.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. This lets you stop faster and still steer your vehicle.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to let a train pass before crossing. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing, as your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing it. What can you do?

options.text: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross them to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Never cross them under any circumstances.
Cross them only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross them only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Sound your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of the car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially when children are nearby.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They move faster and have dimmer lights. Always watch carefully for these smaller and more vulnerable road users.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to reach their destination quickly.
Stay closer to the car ahead.
Stay farther from the car ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time:

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The driver on the left can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery:

options.text: After rain has fallen for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
In the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Heat makes this worse by bringing more oil to the surface.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and turn on your signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Your body removes approximately:

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks per hour.
One alcoholic drink per hour.
Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink per hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, what you've eaten, and your overall health.

questions.question: You should be careful when passing a bicycle because:

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic might not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid an object. Always drive carefully near bicycles.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: Who is responsible for the mechanical condition of a vehicle?

options.text: The legal owner of the vehicle.
The mechanic.
The driver.
The insurance company.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: As the driver, you are responsible for keeping the vehicle in good condition, even if you do not own it. Check your vehicle regularly and perform basic maintenance.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, you may pass if:

options.text: It is an emergency.
You are on an expressway.
Traffic is clear.
You are at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep downhill grade ahead.
Winding road ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downhill grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a steep downhill section is coming.

questions.question: An oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left—if the other driver swerves at the last second, you will still crash. Brake firmly to slow down. Every mile per hour you reduce your speed decreases the impact.

questions.question: You see a flashing yellow light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
Get ready to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly and carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and with caution. Look both ways to check for traffic before crossing.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no traffic signals. What should you do?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and watch carefully. Look both ways for trains on all tracks. If you see or hear a train coming, stop a safe distance away and wait until the train passes before crossing.

questions.question: You park uphill on a street with a curb. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your car will roll toward the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and then:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating you.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again in case you missed a car the first time.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking the rules on these signs can result in a penalty.
